inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average from the H1 FY2026 interim diluted-EPS table (9,248,010,364: basic 9,173.2m + 74.8m share awards), excludes 145.6m A-share treasury shares. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count. Buybacks (RMB1,234m FY2025, RMB1,625m H1 FY2026) fund the flat count.
inputs.cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents 49,873 + current wealth management products 7,239 at 2026-06-30 (the company's own 'net balance of cash and WMP' definition, interim MD&A). Lease liabilities (6,193) are EXCLUDED from total_debt under lease treatment (B). Financial assets at amortised cost (27.6bn) are treated as trade-related and left in working capital.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, 'Share-based payment' add-back RMB490m (FY2024 374m); no cash taxes on equity awards disclosed (net-share settlement is not used; awards are satisfied from treasury shares). H1 FY2026 booked a RMB224m SBC reversal on lapsed awards.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1752, Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-23. Statements and all flows are RMB; the H-share quote is HKD. Parity check against the A-share dual listing (600690.SS): RMB19.65 x 1.1752 = HK$23.09 vs observed H-share HK$19.41, a 16% H-share discount to the A-share -- the normal A/H gap for this name, not an FX-direction error. The D-share (690D, Frankfurt, EUR) was not used.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10y China government bond ~1.8% + China equity risk premium ~6.5% (mature-market ERP plus country premium) x beta ~1.0 for a global consumer-durables manufacturer -> cost of equity ~8.3-8.5%. Debt is ~3% pre-tax but the group is net cash, so WACC ~= cost of equity. 8.5% used in ALL three scenarios; cyclicality, tariff and China-saturation risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Full lease payments (RMB1,801m FY2025 = principal + interest, the single 'Lease payments' financing line; H1 FY2026 908m) are charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path at 0.60% of revenue. Lease liabilities (RMB6,193m at 2026-06-30) are therefore EXCLUDED from total_debt, and D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: 8,750 - 1,865 = 6,885 (2.28% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI is deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at an estimated fair value of RMB13,200m: book NCI 9,697 at 2026-06-30, with the India 49% stake restated from its 2,081 book transfer to the 5,591 cash price Haier received for it in June 2026 (+3,510). NCI profit share was 610 in FY2025 (3% of net income) and will rise with India's 49% minority. Calibration: modelled FY0 NOPAT 17,945 vs total net income 20,163 less excluded associate/interest/WMP/dividend/FX income (4,246) plus after-tax finance costs (~2,225) = ~18,140 -- ties within non-operating noise.
inputs.ebitda_definition: Owner EBITDA (pre-SBC, pre-lease, IFRS-16 basis) = company 'adjusted operating profit' (PBT net of bank interest income, FX, investment returns, FVOCI dividends, finance costs and share of associates) + recurring government grants + D&A + SBC. FY2025: 20,504 + 1,316 + 8,750 + 490 = 31,060 = 10.27% of revenue (FY2024 10.56%; H1 FY2026 11.3% seasonally strong, implied H2 FY2025 ~8.9%). Government grants (~RMB1.3bn/yr, every year since FY2020) are recurring operating cash and kept in; FX gains/losses excluded as noise.
inputs.matching_assets_note: Income stripped from the flows and the asset carried in the bridge: (1) bank interest income -> net cash; (2) share of associates' profit RMB1,328m FY2025 (dividends from associates sit in investing, not OCF) -> interests in associates at 21,857 book less a 20% haircut = 17,500 (largely related-party Haier Group finance-company stakes whose cash is not accessible to minority shareholders); (3) FVOCI dividend income 48 -> equity investments at FVTOCI 5,152 at fair value; (4) return on WMP 160 -> WMP 7,239 inside cash. Nothing is both in the flows and in the bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, three-scenario probability-weighted, component engine (owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md for CNY/HKD currency, leases, NCI, matching assets, cyclical risk-once). Haier Smart Home is a global consumer-durables manufacturer (world #1 appliance maker by volume; China ~48% / overseas ~52% of revenue; GE Appliances, Candy, Fisher & Paykel, AQUA, CCR) with a growing HVAC business -- a standard operating company, so no non-FCF route applies. Fresh build: no prior DCF or Drivers file exists for this ticker. FY0 is FY2025 (Dec year-end) while the balance sheet is 2026-06-30; the H1 FY2026 owner FCF (~RMB3bn, ~0.3/share) is thus counted once in June cash and once in the FY2026 flow -- noted, immaterial (~1.5%) and partly offset by the interim dividend paid in H2. Buyback_cash records real financing outflow (RMB1,234m FY2025), not the authorisation. SBC is small but non-zero (0.16% of revenue): house and street bases differ slightly, so band_position is meaningful though narrow. Price is the regular HKEX close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case 10-year average revenue growth. Deliberately far below the 5y revenue CAGR of 7.6% and equity CAGR of 12.2% because H1 FY2026 revenue fell 2.8% (China retail -9.9%, US tariffs), the China market is saturated (>8 appliances/household, replacement-only demand), and FY2020-25 included the CCR/Kwikot acquisitions and the China trade-in subsidy up-cycle.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 12.2% exceeds revenue 5y CAGR 7.6% by >30% (relative): equity compounding was flattered by a payout ratio that only recently rose to 55% and by acquisition-driven goodwill; not used as the forward growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 9,280 -> FY2022 10,482 -> FY2025 15,031. Owner-FCF 5y CAGR (10.1%) is below reported (11.4%) because interest income grew from 438 to 1,631 as the cash pile built -- part of the reported FCF growth is interest on retained cash, not operations. Lease payments (not available for FY2020-22 in the KPI table) are handled in the forward build via lease_cost_pct_path rather than in the historical series.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -2% (H1 -2.8%; management guides the China decline to narrow in H2 on a lower base and the continuing 15% trade-in subsidy); FY2027-29 3-4% as HVAC (+9.6% in FY2025), emerging markets (+24%) and Europe grow against a flat China/US core; fading to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 owner EBITDA 10.27%; FY2026 10.0% on copper, tariffs and the RMB; then +~0.2pp/yr to 11.0% from HVAC mix, Europe Operating Model 2.0, China DTC logistics savings (RMB340m in 2025) and Casarte premiumisation -- back to the FY2024 level, not above it.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 2.9%, FY2023-24 3.5-3.8%; contracted capex rose to 6,319 at H1 FY2026 (Thailand, Kentucky plants for tariff mitigation), so 3.2% near term easing to 3.0%.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax paid 3,980 FY2025 on modelled EBIT 21,884 = 18.2% (statutory 25% less high-tech 15% rates on China subsidiaries); drifts to 19% as Pillar Two top-up applies to low-tax jurisdictions.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer with receivables + inventory > payables: growth consumes cash. FY2025 OCF 26,003 vs NI+D&A 28,913 implies ~-18% capture on the revenue increase; FY2024 ~-5%; -10% used.

scenario_narratives.base: Revenue dips ~2% in FY2026 as China appliance retail falls on the fading trade-in subsidy and GE Appliances absorbs tariffs and weak US housing, then recovers to 3-4% growth for FY2027-29 as the unified HVAC division (24% of revenue, growing high single digits), South/Southeast Asia and the Middle East (+24% in FY2025) and a restructured Europe outgrow a flat China core. Owner EBITDA margin eases to 10.0% in FY2026 on copper and tariffs, then recovers roughly 0.2pp a year to 11.0% -- the FY2024 level -- on HVAC mix, Casarte premiumisation, European Operating Model 2.0 and DTC logistics savings. Capex runs 3.0-3.2% of revenue while the Thailand and Kentucky plants are built; cash tax drifts from 18% to 19% under Pillar Two; working capital consumes 10% of each year's revenue increase. Terminal growth 2.5%, exit capped at 15x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: HVAC scales toward management's one-third-of-revenue target as heat-pump, data-centre cooling and commercial refrigeration (CCR, PROFROID) demand compounds; India (now 51%-owned, with a partner's capital) and South Asia become the third pillar; US tariffs stabilise and a Fed easing cycle revives housing-linked appliance replacement for GE Appliances; Casarte keeps double-digit growth in a premiumising China. Revenue is flat in FY2026 then grows 5-6% for three years, fading to 3%. Margin reaches 12.0% -- above any year in the FY2020-25 history -- on mix and the European turnaround. Terminal growth 3.0%, exit 16x.
scenario_narratives.bear: H1 FY2026 is the template rather than the trough: China retail stays in decline once the national subsidy is withdrawn (a demand cliff like FY2025/H1 FY2026), a price war among Midea, Gree and Haier over a saturated replacement market compresses pricing, US tariffs stay high and GE Appliances' import-dependent lines lose margin, and copper/steel inflation plus RMB appreciation squeeze a 6.5%-net-margin manufacturer. Revenue falls 5% in FY2026 and 1% in FY2027, then grows 1-2%. Owner EBITDA margin slides to 9.0% and stays there; capex stays elevated at 3.2-3.3% as regionalised manufacturing is a structural cost. Terminal growth 2.0%, exit capped at 13x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% and bull cut from 35% to 25%. The bear case is already partly materialising -- H1 FY2026 revenue -2.8% and net profit -12.9%, China retail -9.9% -- and its two drivers (US tariff policy, China subsidy withdrawal) are outside management's control. The bull case requires several independent things to go right at once (HVAC mix shift, India scale-up, US rate relief, tariff stabilisation). Base 50%: the group is net cash, globally diversified and #1 by volume, so solvency is not the question; the dispersion is about growth and margin, which the weights carry rather than the discount rate.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Haier Smart Home is valued as a mature, cyclical, globally diversified consumer-durables manufacturer on an owner-FCF basis: SBC (small) expensed, bank interest, associate profits and investment income stripped from the flows with their source assets carried in the bridge, leases charged as an operating cost, and NCI deducted once at an estimated fair value. The flows are in RMB and discounted at a CNY-built 8.5% in every scenario; the dispersion of outcomes (tariffs, China saturation, HVAC upside) is priced in the three scenarios and a 25/50/25 weighting rather than in the discount rate. Terminal value is capped at 13-16x owner FCF because appliance makers do not sustain premium multiples through a cycle. Per-share values are computed in RMB and converted to HKD at 1.1752 so they compare with the H-share quote; the 16% H-share discount to the A-share is reported, not assumed away.
key_risks_to_valuation: US tariff policy on GE Appliances' imported components and finished goods -- management's most-cited risk; unresolved and outside the company's control
China market saturation and the eventual withdrawal of the national trade-in subsidy, which produced a -9.9% domestic retail print in H1 FY2026 when the prior programme faded
Industry price war (Midea, Gree) in a replacement-only domestic market compressing a ~10% owner EBITDA margin
Commodity inputs (copper spiked Q4 2025-H1 2026, steel, aluminium) and RMB appreciation against USD/EUR revenue

Bridge items are ~RMB28bn of value (3.0/share): associates are related-party finance-company stakes carried at book less 20%, NCI is an estimate, and the June 2026 balance sheet is used against FY2025 flows
Governance: Haier Group influence, combined Chairman/CEO, three major reorganisations in 2025-26, tri-listing (A/H/D) -- reflected in the persistent H-share discount to the A-share
Terminal value is ~55-60% of enterprise value and bound by the exit cap in base and bull; a lower cap or higher WACC moves value materially (see sensitivity grid)
